messages:
SRE Oncall Bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — elevated 5xx rate from canary hosts (db-canary-0..2) for /v1/profile/write. Severity: P1. Paging oncall.
Alex Chen: Oncall here. Seeing lots of Postgres errors in canary logs: `ERROR: column "user_profile" does not exist` on insert path. Canary app image is v3.2.5-canary. Can we stop the rollout and isolate canary traffic?
Deploy Bot: aborting canary rollout for release v3.2.5-canary. Issuing kill-switch on feature flag `feature:new_profile_schema` and scaling canary replicas to 0.
Alex Chen: Acknowledged. Starting immediate scale-down of canary. Command I'm running: `kubectl rollout pause deployment/api-canary && kubectl scale deployment api-canary --replicas=0` — will update when done.
Priya Kapoor: DB eng here. Quick context: the migration that shipped with v3.2.5 added a `user_profile` jsonb column but wasn't feature-gated in the service codepath; canary apps are writing assuming column exists. That explains missing-column errors on canary read/writes against the canary-postgres schema. We need to prevent writes to new column or revert schema change on canary.
Jordan Mills: Confirmed traffic to canary was ~2% routing via traffic-allocator. Affected requests ~14 orgs in the canary cohort, not all producing errors — looks like a read/write codepath mismatch.
Marta Ruiz: CS — heads up, any customer-facing impact yet? We are getting one inbound from a customer in the canary cohort reporting 500s.
Alex Chen: Canary scale-down complete. Traffic rebalanced to stable. Feature flag kill-switch request submitted to LaunchDarkly via UI — status: `OFF` for `feature:new_profile_schema`. Deploy Bot reports: `canary-traffic -> 0%` :white_check_mark:
Priya Kapoor: I'll run a quick, non-destructive rollback on the canary DB schema to restore compatibility: plan is to remove the new column on canary replicas only and revert migration marker. Proposed SQL (canary only):
```
BEGIN;
ALTER TABLE profiles DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS user_profile;
-- mark migration as not applied in canary_migrations table
DELETE FROM schema_migration_log WHERE migration_id = '20260315_add_user_profile' AND node = 'canary';
COMMIT;
```
Doing this on read-replicas first, then the canary primary. Will monitor for errors.
Jordan Mills: Logs show write stacktrace originating in `profile_service::save()` — the codepath attempted to write JSON blob to `user_profile`. Good catch. Will hold release manager in the loop.
Deploy Bot: Rollback executed for canary images, feature flag off, traffic rebalanced. Status: `canary.rollback=complete`, `flag.feature:new_profile_schema=off`.
Alex Chen: Quick customer impact note: ~14 orgs routed to canary, ~5% of their write requests hit 500s during the window (00:12–00:18 UTC). No auth tokens or user PII exposed in logs. CS: recommend reaching out to the few customers in the cohort with a brief note. Suggest wording: "We briefly routed you to a canary release that caused intermittent 500s; traffic has been routed back to a stable release and we're monitoring." Marta — can you handle outreach?
Marta Ruiz: On it. I'll send the template to the affected accounts and paste copy here after sending. :+1:
Alex Chen: Creating incident channel #inc-1902345678 and starting an internal postmortem doc. Leaving incident open for 60m to watch for regressions.
Priya Kapoor: Canary DB cleanup finished — `user_profile` column removed on canary, migration marker cleared. Running health checks now against canary DB with old service image to verify compatibility.
Jordan Mills: Health checks green. No further errors in canary logs after rollback and schema revert. Rolling retrospective follow-up with release engineer to fix migration ordering and gating.
Deploy Bot: Incident lifecycle: acknowledged -> mitigated -> monitoring. Recommended next steps: block current release until migration ordering is fixed and add a preflight that verifies column availability across DB clusters before rollout.
Alex Chen: Handoff to next oncall — @Priya in 25 minutes. I'll prepare a TL;DR for postmortem and assign follow-ups: 1) rollback migration ordering, 2) add canary DB preflight, 3) update deploy runbook with kill-switch steps. Anyone else?
Priya Kapoor: Taking over now. I'll continue monitoring metrics for 30m and then start a follow-up ticket with release owner. If anything spikes, ping me directly. `ack` :eyes:
Customer Success: Thanks team — we'll hold off on wide customer comms until you confirm stable for +30m. Keep us posted.
Alex Chen: Thanks everyone — great fast response. Closing thread when Priya confirms stable window end. :v:
